scenarios.title: Hidden node and inherited descendant projection
steps: Confirm the explicit hidden root and its descendant are absent from Folder Nodes projections
Use the eye beside Root to enable session reveal and inspect the explicit Hidden text badge and inherited source treatment
Disable Apply hidden markers and reload without editing frontmatter
expected: Only Folder Nodes Explorer, Contents, and Graph projections hide the marked subtree
The explicit root has one non-interactive Hidden text badge, no per-node eye, and the descendant shows inherited muted feedback
Session reveal resets on reload and the hidden=true token remains byte-preserved

scenarios.title: Preview-first structure and property migration, selection creation, and sparse ordering
steps: Preview leaf-note and missing-node organization before committing it
Preview legacy Folder Nodes properties, confirm the conflict blocks writes, resolve it, then explicitly migrate
Create a child node from the selected fixture text after confirming creation location, short node name, and alias policy
Exercise before, into, and after placement using the available platform interaction
expected: No Vault write occurs before either explicit preview confirmation
Legacy tokens migrate to one folder-nodes list while unrelated YAML stays unchanged
The modal omits the full Node Note path and raw wikilink while selection replacement still uses the correct Vault-relative wikilink
Manual order uses only order=manual on the parent and child-owned sparse rank tokens

scenarios.title: Leaf affordance, compact Contents header, and stable graph focus
steps: Inspect a complete visual leaf in File Explorer, then add a visible direct file
Open Node Contents for a deep node, toggle one non-empty section, and navigate away and back

Focus a deep graph node and collapse its parent directly and with Collapse to level 1; on desktop also use Alt to collapse the whole branch, and on Android use the equivalent branch action from the node menu.
Select a parent, view its subtree, then select a child without changing scope; explicitly view the child subtree and return to global
Use the icon, expansion handle, context menu and File Explorer reveal; on desktop also exercise keyboard navigation. Inspect matching handle backgrounds and stable expansion anchors.
expected: The hidden canonical note yields a passive dot, and visible content restores the native disclosure arrow
Breadcrumbs contain ancestors only, the current node appears once, empty sections are absent, and section disclosure survives the view session
Direct and whole-branch operations select their card; range collapse moves hidden focus to the nearest visible ancestor in DOM or Canvas rendering
The scope status names its root independently from the selected card; actions name the selected target and disable only for the same root and mode
Selection and expansion agree across renderers; position, scale and toggle keyboard focus survive redraws; File Explorer reveals the targeted folder

scenarios.title: Short context menus and grouped Folder Nodes actions
steps: Open a complete Folder Node menu from Contents, Graph, File Explorer, and its Node Note tab
Open Folder Nodes actions and inspect Open, Appearance, Structure, and Management groups
Inspect first/last sibling, inherited-hidden, native folder, and Node Note surfaces
expected: The first level stays short and native file or folder actions remain present
Boundary reorder actions are disabled and subtree-wide actions use explicit wording
The grouped action panel is keyboard accessible and touch targets are at least 44px

scenarios.title: Current-node icon containment and small-graph viewport anchors
steps: Inspect Node Contents for Geometry and its Emoji, Glyph, Image, and Lucide children in a narrow pane.
Open the Geometry subtree in DOM 2D, expand and collapse branches with the graph smaller than the viewport and then larger than it, and scroll to the upper and left edges.
Repeat appearance checks with Default and Minimal themes in light and dark modes.
expected: Each current-node visual stays inside its left handle without overlapping or clipping the title.
Expansion and collapse preserve the selected node screen position and all graph content remains reachable by scrolling.
Handles and titles remain legible in all four theme and mode combinations.

scenarios.title: Explicit ordering, unmanaged visibility, and stable refresh
steps: Open Placement and verify _Unmanaged/_Unmanaged.md remains visible in the native Explorer.
Move Placement/Move into Placement/Natural using desktop drag or the Move action. Confirm natural ordering is unchanged.
Open Placement/Manual and use Child order to switch between Name and Manual; use the platform reorder action to change a child position.

On desktop compare the equivalent A-after and B-before gaps with hidden nodes revealed, and verify hidden-gap feedback while they are hidden. On Android verify disabled reorder actions in Name mode and enabled actions in Manual mode.
Open Contents and keep a section disclosure focused while its node icon metadata changes; verify focus retention, then edit only a note body and check that the node list stays stable.
expected: Unmanaged same-named Markdown remains visible; ordinary reparenting does not enable manual ordering.
Sorting is explicitly controlled on the parent and the resulting child order persists.
Desktop gaps match their visible destination and reject hidden ambiguities; Android uses the same explicit ordering rules through menus.
Contents remains usable after refresh and unrelated body edits do not reset its node list.

scenarios.title: Passive Explorer disclosures and active-note creation destination
steps: In File Explorer tap or click the passive dot of a complete leaf with no visible contents; then activate its title separately.
Expand and collapse Geometry repeatedly while an unrelated branch is visible. Add a direct file to the leaf and repeat disclosure activation.
Reload with no Explorer folder selected, open Geometry/Emoji/Emoji.md, then switch to Geometry/Glyph/Glyph.md through an already-open note tab and use the Explorer New node button.
expected: The passive dot neither opens a note nor expands the row. The title opens its Node Note once.
Normal disclosures remain native, visible contents restore the arrow, and unrelated rows and scroll position remain stable.
The creation dialog names Geometry/Glyph as the destination after the active-note switch; cancel the dialog after verifying its destination.

scenarios.title: Viewport toolbar, scope and focus remain independent
steps: Open the Geometry subtree in DOM 2D. Select an off-center node and use zoom in, zoom out, percentage reset and Fit.
Switch to 3D and repeat the toolbar operations; inspect the interaction help in a narrow pane.
On Android scroll DOM 2D with one finger and verify that the zoom, percentage and help controls have touch targets at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels.
expected: The percentage updates immediately and reset returns to 100%; zoom preserves the viewport-center anchor.
Fit contains the graph where permitted by readable node sizes without changing the subtree scope or selection.
Toolbar actions do not open a node or change selection, and the toolbar remains usable in a narrow mobile pane.

scenarios.title: Desktop anchors across DOM and Canvas boundaries
steps: In a fresh disposable Vault, run the acceptance provider command Create 501-node viewport fixture, scope the graph to Viewport, and retain the default large-graph threshold of 500.

In DOM 2D, test ordinary wheel scrolling, Ctrl/Cmd+wheel zoom at an off-center card near the upper-left scroll boundary, and blank-space mouse dragging. Test + and - for zoom and 0 for Fit with graph focus, then confirm they do not hijack the search input.
Select Wide and expand it to cross from 3 visible nodes to 501; pan, zoom above 400% and below 65%, then collapse it to return to DOM. Repeat near both zoom limits and all viewport edges.
Repeat expansion, collapse, off-center pointer zoom, percentage reset and Fit in 3D with both renderers.
expected: Unmodified wheel scrolls while Ctrl/Cmd+wheel zooms around its pointer; blank dragging pans without opening nodes.
Selection, scope, supported zoom and the expansion-card screen anchor survive both renderer transitions without a visible jump.
Zoom limits do not move the anchored point, all graph content remains reachable, and search typing retains normal text behavior.
3D pointer zoom preserves its projected anchor and both renderers expose the same toolbar actions.

scenarios.title: Android native pinch and two-finger pan across graph renderers
steps: Confirm the input host receives two simultaneous native touch pointers with distinct identities and releases both after cancellation or completion.

Generate the 501-node Viewport fixture in a fresh disposable Vault and expand Wide to enter Canvas 2D. Pinch at an off-center midpoint, translate both fingers together, then combine scaling and translation.
Repeat in DOM 3D with Wide collapsed and Canvas 3D with Wide expanded. Exercise zoom limits, toolbar reset, Fit and expansion across the 500-node renderer boundary.
After each two-finger gesture, lift both fingers and tap or long-press a card normally. In DOM 2D use native one-finger scrolling and toolbar zoom.
expected: Pinch preserves the world point under its moving midpoint and same-distance two-finger movement pans without rotating the 3D camera.
Two-finger gestures do not accidentally select, open or invoke a context menu for a node.
Supported zoom and selected-card position remain stable across renderer changes; percentage and controls stay synchronized.
No pointer remains captured after release or cancellation, and ordinary interaction resumes.
